title: Two Gaia DR3 acceleration detections remain linked to TESS timing changes in tests that control brightness, parallax and observing coverage
abstract: We test whether measured Gaia selection variables explain the astrometric excess in a published sample of southern eclipsing binaries. New Gaia DR3 queries reproduce 14 robust timing systems and 393 quiet controls. Two timing systems have acceleration solutions; the quiet detection is variability-induced motion, not acceleration. Six conditional designs with magnitude, parallax and transit coverage give acceleration probabilities from 0.00027 to 0.00893. Five matched controls per timing system give 0.02778. An unmeasured within-set odds factor of 1.44 can raise the worst-case matched probability to 0.05. The tested measured variables do not remove the excess, but only two stars carry it. This is a selection audit, not orbit confirmation or a triple-fraction estimate.

display.caption: Conditional association tests and aggregate control balance. Small matched sets have less power; the evidence comes from two acceleration detections.

citations.reason: Timing classes and Gaia comparison. New selection tests support the excess; the quiet Gaia detection is VIM rather than acceleration.
